NOTE: The tumor is composed of both malignant epithelial and mesenchymal (sarcomatous) areas. These two components are distinct and do not show any merging from the carcinoma into the sarcoma. Immunoperoxidase stains confirm divergent differentiation, with cytokeratins being positive only in the epithelial areas and vimentin and desmin only in the sarcomatous regions. S-100 only stains the carcinoma. Although the differential diagnosis includes a metaplastic carcinoma with extensive sarcomatous areas, there is usually more blending of the epithelial and mesenchymal areas in metaplastic carcinoma. Also, immunoperoxidase usually shows some keratin-positivity in the sarcomatous areas in a metaplastic carcinoma. Another interesting feature in this case is that the background of this tumor is reminiscent of a phylloides tumor, with broad stromal fronds focally covered by malignant epithelium. This feature raises the possibility that this tumor is arising in a high-grade phylloides. All margins are greater than 0.2cm. No angiolymphatic invasion is seen. Dr. Koerner has reviewed the case and agrees with this interpretation.
